'''''Delosperma''''' ('delos'=evident, 'sperma'=seed) is a [[genus]] of around 170 [[species]] of [[succulent plant]]s, formerly included in ''[[Mesembryanthemum]]'' in the family [[Aizoaceae]]. It was defined by English botanist [[N. E. Brown]] in 1925.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.2307/1221621|jstor=1221621|title=The Lectotype of ''Delosperma'' N. E. Brown (Aizoaceae) |last1=Taylor |first1=Nigel |last2=Eggli |first2=Urs |journal=Taxon |year=1986 |volume=35 |issue=4 |pages=709–711}}</ref> The genus is common in southern and eastern Africa, with a few species in [[Madagascar]], [[Reunion island]], [[Yemen]] and [[Saudi Arabia]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Smith |first=G.F. |date=1998 |title=Mesembs of the world |publisher=Briza Publications |page=292}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Hartmann |first=Heidrun E. K. |date=2017 |title=Aizoaceae - Second Edition |publisher=Springer |page=395}}</ref> ''Delosperma'' species, as do most [[Aizoaceae]], have [[hygrochastic]] capsules, opening and closing as they wet and dry.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Origami-like unfolding of hydro-actuated ice plant seed capsules |doi=10.1038/ncomms1336 |pmid=21654637 |bibcode=2011NatCo...2..337H |year=2011|journal=Nat. Commun.|vauthors=Harrington MJ, Razghandi K, Ditsch F, Guiducci L, Rueggeberg M, Dunlop JW, Fratzl P, Neinhuis C, Burgert I|volume=2|page=337|doi-access=free}}</ref>
[[Image:Delosperma tradescantioides leafs IMGP0042.jpg|thumb|right|The leaves of ''Delosperma jansei (tradescantioides?)'']]

==Distinguishing characters==
Plants of the genus ''Delosperma'' can be distinguished by their seed capsules. When these open (in response to rain), the seeds are exposed and not covered by a protective membrane, like those of most other plants in the family. The membrane is sometimes reduced to just a ledge (a feature shared by the related genus ''[[Trichodiadema]]''. The triangular valves, which open outwards when wet, each have distinctive wings on either side.

''Delosperma'' leaves tend to be grooved or covered in bladder cells, which are sometimes even extended into hairs. The leaf shape is cylindrical or sometimes flattened.<ref>[http://pza.sanbi.org/delosperma Delosperma - SANBI]</ref>

''Delosperma'' species are long-lived, and flower mostly in the summer. Their flowers vary greatly in colour.
